project.name: Dashboard UX Sprint C — Insight Completeness & Opportunity Assessment Quality

summary: Sprint C addresses the critical gaps identified in a systematic end-to-end review against five evaluation criteria (speed to insight, opportunity completeness, analytical depth, data credibility, client readiness). Key changes: Overview gains Tail Spend KPI, clickable charts that navigate to relevant pages, and a concentration stat. Recommendations page gets a hero savings number, priority matrix legend, and a fixed confidence filter position. Supplier table gains payment days colour coding and WC opportunity column. Category page shows top suppliers within the selected L1. Data Quality replaces the score card with a narrative summary strip and fixes the inverted progress bar direction. Payment Terms gains a 100% stacked distribution bar. Sidebar nav is reordered to match the opportunity assessment workflow. All frontend-only.

decisions.tail_spend_replaces_invoice_count: OverviewData already has tail_spend_pct field. Invoice Count is an operational metric, not a procurement diagnostic. Tail Spend % directly answers a standard category manager question.
decisions.chart_navigation: Overview supplier bar onBarClick navigates to /supplier page. Treemap onCellClick navigates to /category page. Both use useNavigate() from react-router-dom. No pre-filter state needed — the user lands on the page and can drill in.
decisions.data_freshness_label: OverviewData.data_freshness field exists in the TypeScript type. If it returns an ISO date string from the backend, format it with formatDate(). If null, omit the label.
decisions.concentration_stat: Computed client-side from already-fetched supplierData. Top 10 suppliers = sum of top-10 total_spend / total of all supplierData. Displayed as a text line below the supplier bar chart title.
decisions.savings_hero: Total Identified Savings rendered as a standalone display above the 4-card KPI grid on the Recommendations page. 5xl font-bold text-green-700. This is the most important number on the page and deserves visual primacy.
decisions.priority_matrix_legend: A simple flex row of colored dot + label pairs rendered below the ScatterChart. One entry per lever in leverSummaries order, using CHART_COLORS[leverIndex]. No new dependency.
decisions.payment_days_colour: Cells in payment days columns: <30 days bg-rose-50 text-rose-700, 30-44 bg-amber-50 text-amber-700, >=45 no extra class (already good terms). Applied in both SupplierPage table and PaymentTermsPage table.
decisions.category_top_suppliers: When L1 selected, fetch /cube/by-supplier with params { category_l1: selectedL1 }. Backend may not filter by category — if so, returns all engagement suppliers, still useful as a starting point. Show top 5 by total_spend as a mini table below the L2 bar chart.
decisions.data_quality_narrative: Replace isolated max-w-xs score card with a full-width summary strip showing counts: X passing, X warnings, X issues. The strip uses coloured counter badges (green/amber/red) and is more scannable than a single score percentage.
decisions.stacked_bar_payment_terms: Recharts BarChart in horizontal layout with one Bar per bucket, stacked, showing percentage of total spend. No new component — render inline in PaymentTermsPage using recharts directly. The existing bucket vertical bar chart is replaced.
decisions.nav_reorder: New order matches opportunity assessment workflow: Overview → Recommendations → Category → Supplier → Payment Terms → Quality. Review Workstation stays at bottom.
decisions.selected_bar_highlight: Add selectedLabel prop to SpendBarChart. When a bar's name matches selectedLabel, render it with a darker/fuller opacity and a 2px border stroke. Other bars get opacity 0.7.
decisions.no_backend_changes: All frontend-only. Uses existing API endpoints with optional query params that may or may not be supported by the backend.
